set.body:
Problem:
Sojourn SiteOperation and OperationDescriptor mirror scala-slurm OperationRef and RegisteredOperation, while OperationRegistry and TaskRegistry independently validate and store nearly the same registrations. WorkerBridge copies fields between these parallel models and the Sojourn registry contains audited erasure casts.

Scope:
- Select one neutral typed operation reference and one untyped wire descriptor.
- Define one registration value that owns operation identity, schemas, codecs, retry safety, and the effectful implementation while preserving the separation between portable descriptor and executable registration.
- Derive the public operation catalog, local runner lookup, one-shot worker registry, and pilot registry from the same validated registrations.
- Remove structural field-copy adapters and duplicate conflict rules.

Acceptance criteria:
- Exactly one production definition owns the id, version, input schema, and result schema tuple.
- Site, batch, local, one-shot worker, and pilot paths consume derived views of one registration source.
- WorkerBridge.operationRef or any equivalent field-by-field identity copy is removed.
- Duplicate id/version registrations, mismatched schemas, and divergent implementations fail once at registry construction with typed diagnostics.
- No production asInstanceOf or unchecked pattern is required to recover operation input/output types in the registry or worker bridge.
- Registry/catalog construction is deterministic and order-independent for valid inputs.
- Tests prove the same operation and codecs execute identically through local batch, local pool, and one-shot worker paths, including raised task errors and codec failures.
- Public migration notes identify renamed or removed operation APIs.
- Full Sojourn TCK and scala-slurm worker/protocol suites pass.
set.title: SCOMP.2: Use one operation descriptor and registry model
